Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. Alyssa Healy, for one final time in ODIs, gives an inspirational pep-talk in a huddle before the team disperse. Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana to open for India. The focus shifts from Alyssa Healy to the debutant, Lucy Hamilton. Two slips in place as Hamilton steams in.
...THE CHASE...

Can India chase it down? For India, it was a day of being completely outclassed. They did make a slight comeback in the final moments of the innings, but it was nullified by a 22-run penultimate over from Sree Charani. India already looked tired, and their shoulders were drooping. Smriti Mandhana was having a back message in the middle of an over, indicating she was in some pain. Can she give a fitting start to a mountainous total India are chasing? Stay tuned to find out.

A fitting farewell -  Once the spinners were introduced, the narrative remained unchanged. There was no respite, no tightening of the screws, only an Australian side intent on destruction. Alyssa Healy and Georgia Voll laid the foundation with a blistering 104-run partnership, and even after Voll departed, India’s misery only compounded. Beth Mooney strode to the crease to join an already set Healy, and together, they dismantled the bowling attack with chilling efficiency, piling on 145 runs in just 92 deliveries.

Healy's final bow - It began with a moment of pure class. The Indian side formed a corridor of respect, a guard of honour for a woman who has defined an era. But once the pleasantries ended and the first ball was delivered, the sentimentality was packed away. Alyssa Healy didn’t just walk out to play an innings, she walked out to put on a masterclass.  The new-ball pairing of Renuka Singh Thakur and Kashvee Gautam struggled to find their rhythm, failing to extract the swing they desperately needed. Australia sensed that fragility immediately, capitalising on the lack of movement to plunder 69 runs in the Powerplay alone. It set the tone for a brutal onslaught.

We have witnessed something special. A Sunday to remember, and a farewell for the ages at the Bellerive Oval. It was a day when Harmanpreet Kaur’s luck began and ended with the toss of a coin. It was a day when all eyes were on Alyssa Healy, and her last ODI appearance at the Bellerive Oval was nothing short of legendary. However, Beth Mooney's innings was overshadowed by Alyssa Healy's early knock, which was of equal importance as Australia fell off track in the fag end, only for Mooney to score a wonderful century and get the total over 400.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. There was a bit of cloud cover during the toss, but it has now given way to bright sunshine. The Indian players line up to give Alyssa Healy a guard of honour as she walks out to open the batting in her final ODI. Phoebe Litchfield will be her opening partner. Renuka Singh Thakur will kickstart proceedings with the new ball. Thakur to Healy with a slip in place. Let's go...

India Women (Playing XI) - Pratika Rawal, Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol (In for Amanjot Kaur), Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana (In for Vaishnavi Sharma), Richa Ghosh (WK), Kashvee Gautam, Sree Charani and Renuka Singh Thakur (In for Kranti Gaud).

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C), Phoebe Litchfield, Georgia Voll, Beth Mooney (WK), Annabel Sutherland, Ashleigh Gardner, Tahlia McGrath, Georgia Wareham (In for Darcie Brown), Nicola Carey, Lucy Hamilton (On ODI debut) (In for Megan Schutt) and Alana King.

Debut for a 19-year-old - Australia's skipper, Alyssa Healy informs that Lucy Hamilton is making her debut today, and she wants the game to be more about the debutant. Feels it is a nice little glimpse into Australia’s future. She further says that Georgia Wareham also comes into the side. Healy shares that it has been a whirlwind couple of weeks for Hamilton, and she is eager to see what she can produce. Mentions that she has thoroughly enjoyed representing Australia and adds that she will be able to reflect more properly on her career next week.

Spin to win - That's the mantra for the game for the Indian captain. Harmanpreet Kaur starts by saying she is not used to winning tosses. Kaur says they are going to bowl first as she feels the pitch is a bit dry and the spinners will do the job. Informs that they have made three changes. Kranti Gaud, Vaishnavi Sharma and Amanjot Kaur are resting while Harleen Deol, Renuka Singh Thakur and Sneh Rana feature in the XI.
TOSS - All set for the coin to go up. Alyssa Healy, in her last ODI, is standing alongside Harmanpreet Kaur. Kaur wins the 6th straight toss of the series. India elect to BOWL first.

Debut alert - Australia will make at least one change, with Lucy Hamilton all set to make her ODI debut. The left-arm quick has received her maiden cap from skipper Alyssa Healy. Lucy was the leading wicket taker for Brisbane Heat during last year's WBBL and was among the few bright spots in a challenging campaign where Brisbane finished at the bottom of the table. Hamilton becomes the 151st player to represent Australia in Women's ODIs.

India searching for answers - The ODI champions have struggled to pose a serious challenge. Underwhelming batting performances in both matches have left them playing catch-up, while inconsistency with the ball has made it difficult to build sustained pressure. Untidy fielding has further compounded their issues. India have now lost their last five ODIs on Australian soil. They will be eager to end that streak, restore confidence, and carry some much-needed momentum into the one-off Test. Stick around for the toss and team news.

Australia in control - Despite dealing with a number of injuries in their camp, the home side has remained composed and clinical, sealing the first two ODIs with authority. They were uncharacteristically sloppy in the field in the previous game and will be keen to tighten up in that department. Having played 5 white ball matches in 13 days, they may choose to rest a couple of players to manage workloads ahead of the upcoming Test.

Hello from Hobart - We are back at the Bellerive Oval as Australia and India meet for one final time in this ODI series, with the hosts leading the multi-format contest 6-4. The Aussies will be eager to stretch that advantage to an unassailable margin in what will be their inspirational leader, Alyssa Healy's final ODI appearance, while India will be determined to level the series before attention shifts to the one-off Test next week.

Match intro - As the multi-format tour reaches its penultimate stage, the focus shifts back to the Bellerive Oval in Hobart for the third and final One Day International between Australia Women and India Women. With the ICC Women’s Championship points at stake and a historic Test match in Perth looming, this clash between the world’s two most formidable sides carries weight far beyond a simple bilateral result. The series has been a tactical chess match. Australia, the relentless juggernaut at home, has relied on their trademark depth and clinical finishing. India, however, arrived with momentum from a T20I series win (2-1) and the psychological edge of their historic 2025 World Cup semi-final victory over the Aussies but haven't been able to translate the same form in this WODI series this far. Australia's resilience - The hosts have had to navigate significant injury concerns. With Ellyse Perry and Kim Garth sidelined due to quad injuries, and captain Sophie Molineux recently ruled out with a lower back issue, the invincible Aussie squad looks more human than usual. However, the emergence of Phoebe Litchfield and Georgia Voll, along with the steady hand of Beth Mooney ensure the Southern Stars remain favorites on home soil. India's quest for consistency - For Harmanpreet Kaur’s side, the tour has been a rollercoaster. While the T20I victory was a statement of intent, the transition to the 50-over format has tested their middle-order stability. Smriti Mandhana remains the linchpin and her record against Australia is sensational. If the opening pair of Mandhana and Pratika Rawal can survive the Powerplay, India has the firepower to post or chase a big total. Pitch and conditions - The Bellerive Oval is known for its true bounce and short square boundaries, making it a batter's paradise once the initial moisture evaporates.
